crane.definition: A large machine used by trained operators to lift and move heavy loads.

bulldozer.definition: A heavy vehicle with a broad front blade for moving earth.

excavator.definition: A machine with a powered arm and bucket for digging and moving earth.

dump-truck.definition: A truck with a container that tilts to unload loose material.

cement-mixer.definition: A rotating machine for mixing concrete ingredients; often called a concrete mixer.

forklift.definition: A powered industrial vehicle with forks for lifting and moving loads.

steamroller.definition: A heavy roller used to compact surfaces; modern machines need not be steam-powered.

backhoe.definition: A digging machine or attachment with a bucket pulled toward the operator.

pile-driver.definition: A machine used to drive long support piles into the ground.

boom-lift.definition: A machine with an extending arm and platform for authorized work at height.

brick.definition: A shaped building block commonly made of fired clay.

cement.definition: A binding material that forms part of concrete and mortar.

steel-beam.definition: A structural steel member supporting loads in a building.

plywood.definition: A board made from thin layers of wood bonded together.

glass-pane.definition: A flat sheet of glass used in a window or similar structure.

pipe.definition: A hollow tube used to carry liquids, gases, or other materials.

cable.definition: A group of wires or strands forming a strong line or electrical connection.

bolt.definition: A threaded metal fastener commonly used with a nut.

nail.definition: A pointed metal fastener driven into a material.

screw.definition: A fastener with a spiral thread that turns into material.

drywall.definition: Building panels used to form interior walls and ceilings.

hammer.definition: A hand tool with a heavy head used for striking.

wrench.definition: A tool used to turn nuts and bolts.

screwdriver.definition: A tool used to turn screws.

drill.definition: A tool with a rotating bit used to make holes.

saw.definition: A tool with a toothed blade used for cutting material.

tape-measure.definition: A flexible marked strip used for measuring distances.

level.definition: A tool used to check whether a surface is horizontal or vertical.

pliers.definition: A two-handled tool used for gripping or bending material.

chisel.definition: A cutting tool with a sharp edge used to shape hard material.

utility-knife.definition: A small cutting tool with a sharp replaceable or retractable blade.

allen-key.definition: A hexagonal tool used to turn screws with a matching socket.

socket-set.definition: A collection of detachable sockets for turning nuts and bolts.

hard-hat.definition: A rigid protective helmet worn on a work site.

safety-vest.definition: A high-visibility garment helping workers be seen.

steel-toe-boots.definition: Work boots with protective steel reinforcement over the toes.

safety-goggles.definition: Protective eyewear selected to shield the eyes from work hazards.

ear-plugs.definition: Small inserts worn to reduce noise reaching the ears.

dust-mask.definition: A face covering intended to reduce exposure to certain airborne particles; suitability depends on its rating and the hazard.

harness.definition: A system of straps worn as part of approved work-at-height protection.

safety-net.definition: A professionally installed net used as part of a fall-protection system.

caution-tape.definition: Marked tape used to indicate a restricted area or possible hazard.

traffic-cone.definition: A cone-shaped marker used to guide movement or mark an area.

scaffolding.definition: A temporary structure providing access and support for authorized building work.

foundation.definition: The lower structural part transferring a building’s load to the ground.

frame.definition: The supporting structural skeleton of a building.

roof-truss.definition: A framework of connected members supporting a roof.

concrete-slab.definition: A flat structural section made from concrete.

ramp.definition: A sloping surface connecting different heights.

fence.definition: A barrier marking or enclosing an area.

gate.definition: A movable barrier allowing entry through a fence or wall.

container.definition: A large enclosed unit used for storage or transport.

portable-toilet.definition: A movable toilet unit used where permanent facilities are unavailable.

architect.definition: A professional who designs buildings and related spaces.

engineer.definition: A professional applying technical knowledge to design or evaluate systems and structures.

foreman.definition: A worker responsible for supervising a crew on a site.

electrician.definition: A qualified worker who installs or maintains electrical systems.

plumber.definition: A qualified worker who installs or repairs water and drainage systems.

carpenter.definition: A skilled worker who builds or repairs wooden structures and fittings.

bricklayer.definition: A skilled worker who lays bricks to build walls and other structures.

painter.definition: A worker who applies paint or protective coatings to surfaces.

welder.definition: A skilled worker who joins materials, usually metal, using a welding process.

crane-operator.definition: A trained worker who operates a crane.

steel.definition: A strong metal alloy made mainly from iron and carbon.

wood.definition: Material obtained from trees and used for building and other purposes.

glass.definition: A hard transparent or translucent material used in windows and other building features.

blueprint.definition: A technical drawing showing a building’s design; modern copies are not necessarily blue.
